title: Vector Databases
content: Vector databases store high-dimensional numerical vectors and enable fast similarity search at scale. Unlike traditional databases that match exact values
column4: vector databases find the nearest neighbours to a query vector using metrics like cosine similarity or Euclidean distance. They are the backbone of semantic search and RAG pipelines.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a retrieval step with a language model. A query is embedded into a vector and used to fetch relevant documents from a vector store. Those documents are passed as context to an LLM
column4: grounding its response in factual content and reducing hallucinations.

title: Transformer Architecture
content: The Transformer architecture introduced multi-head self-attention to replace recurrent networks. Each token attends to all other tokens in the sequence
column4: capturing long-range dependencies efficiently. Transformers are the foundation of modern language models including BERT

title: BERT Embeddings
content: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) produces contextual embeddings by reading text in both directions. Fine-tuned variants like bge-small and all-MiniLM are commonly used for semantic similarity tasks. The [CLS] token or mean-pooled hidden states are used as sentence-level embeddings.

title: Cosine Similarity
content: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors
column4: returning 1 for identical directions and 0 for orthogonal vectors. It ignores vector magnitude and focuses purely on direction
column5: making it ideal for comparing L2-normalised embeddings. Most embedding models are trained to maximise cosine similarity between semantically related texts.

title: Apache Arrow
content: Apache Arrow defines a language-independent columnar memory format for flat and hierarchical data. It enables zero-copy reads between systems and is the in-memory format used by DataFusion
column5: and many analytics engines. Arrow arrays are the native exchange format in Skardi pipelines.

title: DataFusion Query Engine
content: DataFusion is an in-process SQL query engine written in Rust
column4: built on Apache Arrow. It supports vectorised execution
column6: and custom scalar UDFs and table functions. Skardi uses DataFusion as its query engine
column7: allowing SQL to be extended with ML inference UDFs like candle() and onnx_predict().

title: Lance Format
content: Lance is a columnar storage format optimised for machine learning workloads. It supports random-access reads
column5: and built-in ANN (approximate nearest-neighbour) indexing for vector columns. Skardi uses Lance as its primary vector store
column6: accessed via the lance_knn() table function.

title: Semantic Search
content: Semantic search retrieves documents based on meaning rather than keyword overlap. A query and all documents are embedded into the same vector space; the most semantically similar documents are returned via nearest-neighbour search. This handles synonyms and paraphrases that would confuse keyword search.

title: SQL in ML Pipelines
content: Expressing ML pipelines in SQL keeps logic declarative and auditable. Features like CTEs
column5: and window functions compose naturally with UDFs for model inference. Skardi extends standard SQL with candle() for local embedding and onnx_predict() for general ONNX model inference.

title: Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search
content: Exact nearest-neighbour search scales as O(n) per query. ANN algorithms like HNSW and IVF-PQ trade a small accuracy loss for sub-linear query times
column4: making billion-scale vector search practical. Lance builds HNSW indices on vector columns for fast ANN queries via lance_knn().

title: SafeTensors Format
column4: safe format for storing neural network weights developed by HuggingFace. Unlike pickle-based PyTorch checkpoints
column5: SafeTensors files cannot execute arbitrary code on load. Candle loads model weights exclusively from SafeTensors files.

title: Mean Pooling
content: Mean pooling aggregates the per-token hidden states from a transformer encoder into a single fixed-size vector. Each token embedding is averaged across the sequence length
column4: yielding a sentence embedding. It outperforms [CLS]-token pooling for most semantic similarity tasks.

title: L2 Normalisation
content: L2 normalisation scales a vector so its Euclidean norm equals 1. After normalisation
column4: cosine similarity between two vectors equals their dot product
column5: which is faster to compute. Most embedding models recommend normalising output vectors before indexing or querying a vector store.

title: Quantised Models
content: Quantised models reduce weight precision from float32 to int8 or lower
column4: shrinking model size and speeding up inference. GGUF is a popular quantised format for running large models on CPU. Candle supports GGUF loading
column5: making it possible to run quantised embedding models without a GPU.
